senses.gloss: शिक्षित, शिक्षु, &c. See p. 1004, col. 3.

शिक्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, learnt, studied; instructed,
taught (with acc., e. g. शिक्षितो नृत्यम्, instructed
in dancing); disciplined, exercised, trained, tamed,
tame; docile; skilful, clever, conversant; modest, diffi-
dent.
—शिक्षिताक्षर (˚त-अक्˚), अस्, m. one who is
taught letters or literature, a pupil, scholar.
—शिक्षि-
तायुध (˚त-आय्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, skilled in weapons.

शिक्कु शिक्कु, उस्, उस्, उ, idle, lazy, following
no business or profession.

शिक्थ शिक्थ or शिक्थक, अम्, n. bee's
wax, (also written सिक्थक, q. v.)

शिक्य शिक्य, अम्, आ, n. f. (according to
Uṇādi-s. V. 16. fr. शि substituted for rt. स्रंस्, cf.
शिच्), a kind of loop or swing made of rope and
suspended from either end of a pole or yoke to
receive a load; the burden or load so carried; a sort
of hanging-shelf suspended by strings; the strings of
a balance.
—शिक्याधार (˚या-आध्˚), अस्, m. ‘loop-
holder,’ the hook or eye at each end of a pole or
beam for holding the above looped cord or for hold-
ing the strings of a balance.

शिक्यित, अस्, आ, अम्, placed or carried in the above
loop, suspended in a swing or loop made of cord, &c.

शिक्वन् शिक्वन् (perhaps connected with
शिक्य above), Ved. a rope, cord, (Sāy. शिक्वभिः =
रज्जुभिः, Ṛg-veda I. 141, 8.)

शिक्वस् शिक्वस् (connected with rt. 1. शक्),
Ved. mighty, powerful, able, (Sāy. शिक्वसः = शक्-
ताः, Ṛg-veda V. 52, 16; शिक्वसे = शक्ताय, Ṛg-
veda X. 92, 9.)

शिक्ष् शिक्ष् (properly Desid. of rt. 1. शक्,
q. v., but regarded by some as a separate rt.), cl. 1. A.
शिक्षते, Aor. अशिक्षिष्ट, शिक्षितुम्, to learn,
acquire knowledge; to teach (Ved.); to give (P.,
Ved., see rt. 1. शक्): Pass. शिक्ष्यते, Aor. अशिक्षि:
Caus. शिक्षयति, -ते, Aor. अशिशिक्षत्, -त, to teach,
&c., (see rt. 1. शक्, p. 985.)

शिक्षक, अस्, आ or इका, अम्, a learner; a teacher,
instructor, (in this sense fr. Caus.); one who knows
Śikṣā or the science of euphony, (see below.)

शिक्षण, अम्, n. the act of learning, acquiring
knowledge; teaching, instruction (fr. Caus.).
शिक्षाण, अस्, आ, अम्, learning, acquiring knowledge.

शिक्षणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be learnt; to be taught
(fr. Caus.).
शिक्षत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. teaching, instructing.

सीक्षत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (fr. a Vedic Desid.), Ved.
desiring to overcome, anxious to conquer, (Sāy. =
सोढुम्, i. e. अभिभवितुम् इच्छत्, Ṛg-veda VI.
14, 3.)
सीक्षत् सीक्षत्. See p. 1100, col. 1.

शिक्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. learning; (अस्),
m. a learner, pupil.

शिक्षयितृ, ता, m. (fr. Caus.), an instructor,
teacher.
शिक्षयित्वा, ind. having taught, having instructed.

शिक्षा, f. desire of being able to effect anything,
wish to prevail (Kirāt. XV. 37); learning, study,
the acquisition of knowledge; teaching, instruction,
training, discipline; the science which teaches proper
pronunciation and especially the laws of euphony
peculiar to the Veda, (one of the six Vedāṅgas; see
वेदाङ्ग); modesty, humility, diffidence; giving,
bestowing (Ved., see rt. 1. शक्); the plant Bignonia
Indica.
—शिक्षा-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, instruction-caus-
ing, instruction-giving; (अस्), m. a teacher, instructor;
[]
epithet of Vyāsa.
—शिक्षा-गुरु, उस्, m. a religious
preceptor, teacher.
—शिक्षा-नर, अस्, m., Ved. the
chief or foremost in liberality; epithet of Indra,
(Sāy. = दानस्य नेता.)
—शिक्षा-शक्ति, इस्, f.
‘power of learning,’ dexterity, skill.
—शिक्षा-सूत्र,
अम्, n., N. of a section in the Kātantra treating of
the pronunciation of letters.

शिक्षितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be learnt; to be in-
structed or taught.
शिक्षित्वा, ind. having learnt; having instructed.
शिक्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, learning; instructing.

शिक्षु, उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of learning, one who
wishes to learn.

शिक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be learnt; to be trained
or taught, teachable.
सिक्ष्य सिक्ष्य, अस्, m. crystal, glass.

शिक्ष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being learnt; being
taught; (अस्), m. a pupil.

शीक् शीक् (also written सीक्, and per-
haps connected with rt. 1. सिच्), cl. 1.
A. शीकते, शिशीके, शीकिष्यते, अशीकिष्ट, शीकितुम्,
to sprinkle, wet, moisten; to go gently, move; cl.
1. 10. P. शिकति, शीकयति, to bear ill or impatiently,
be angry; to bear patiently, be patient; to touch
(= rt. चीक्); to speak (cl. 10); to shine (cl. 10).

सिक् सिक्, a Sautra rt. meaning ‘to
scatter about, sprinkle;’ [cf. rts. 1. सिच्,
सीक्.]

सीक् सीक् (also written शीक्, q. v.), cl. 1.
A. सीकते, &c., to sprinkle, scatter in
drops, (in which sense the form सीक् seems preferable
to शीक्, cf. rts. सिक्, 1. सिच्); to go, move; cl. 1. 10.
P. सीकति, सीकयति, &c., to be impatient; to be
patient; to touch, &c. (see rt. शीक्).

शीकर, अस्, m. thin or drizzling rain, drizzle,
spray, mist, rain driven by wind; a drop of rain or
water, (also written सीकर); (अम्), n. the resin of
the Sarala pine or the tree itself.
—शीकरौघ
(˚र-ओघ), अस्, आ, अम्, abounding with mist, having
much spray or thin rain.

सीकर, अस्, m. drizzling rain, drizzle, mist, &c.;
(see शीकर, but the form सीकर seems preferable.)
शिकरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, sprinkling, drizzling.

सिकत, आस्, m. pl. (said to be fr. the Sautra rt.
above; probably fr. rt. 1. सिच्), sand; N. of certain
Ṛṣis, (part of the hymn Ṛg-veda IX. 86. is attri-
buted to Sikatāḥ); (आ), f. sandy soil; sand; gravel
or stone (the disease).
—सिकता-मय, अस्, ई, अम्,
consisting of sand, full of sand, sandy; (अम्), n. a
sand-bank; an island with sandy shores.
—सिकता-
रेणु, उस्, m. a grain of sand.
—सिकता-वत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, possessed of sand, abounding in sand, sandy.
सिकतिल, अस्, आ, अम्, sandy (as a soil, country, &c.).
सिक्त सिक्त, सिक्थ, &c. See col. 2.
सिक्ति, इस्, f. sprinkling; effusion; emission.

सिक्त्वा, ind. having sprinkled, having poured out
or effused.
सिक्थक, अम्, n. bee's-wax.
